title: Markets move before the news arrives
hook: The recession started in 2008 — so why did stocks top out in 2007?
metaphor: Markets are a room full of people betting on next year's weather. They act on the forecast, not on today's rain.
body: Investors try to guess the economy six to nine months ahead.
So prices turn before the official numbers turn.
By the time a recession is announced, markets often already fell.
This is why waiting for confirmation usually means arriving late.

caveat: Markets guess wrong often. They have predicted far more downturns than actually happened.
